app.name: Focos
app.title: Focos: a fire calendar for Argentina
app.description: See when any area of Argentina burns, which years were worst and whether this month is unusual. One record since 2003, harmonized from NASA MODIS and VIIRS hotspots and tested on held-out years.
app.tagline: One fire calendar for Argentina from MODIS and VIIRS, since 2003
app.lede: MODIS and VIIRS count fires differently. Focos converts VIIRS to MODIS-equivalent hotspots, tested on years it never saw, so every year since 2003 can be compared.

question.heading: 1. The question
question.p1: Argentina’s fire record comes from two kinds of satellite sensor. MODIS on the Aqua satellite has reported hotspots since 2002. VIIRS, which flies on S-NPP since 2012 and on NOAA-20 since 2018, sees smaller fires, so it reports several times as many for the same fire season.
question.p2: Aqua is drifting in its orbit and is at the end of its life, so the record has to move to VIIRS. Can two records that count differently be read as one?

naive.heading: 2. The naive answer, and why it fails
naive.text: The simple answer is to put the VIIRS counts after the MODIS counts. That draws a jump no fire caused: in {year}, the first year both sensors flew, VIIRS reported {viirs} detections where Aqua’s record counts {aqua} fire cell-passes. Any trend read across that jump is false.
naive.caption: Hotspots in Argentina per year. The harmonized VIIRS line is the record Focos shows.
naive.label: Yearly national totals from {from} to {to}: Aqua MODIS, raw VIIRS and harmonized VIIRS.

steps.heading: 3. The method, in three steps
steps.s1: Clean both sensors the same way. Keep only the detections the archive labels as vegetation fire, which drops the gas flares and other fixed heat sources it has labelled (not every one is labelled; see Limits), drop low-confidence detections, and give every detection its local date.
steps.s2: Count both sensors the same way. The unit is a fire cell-pass: one cell of about 1 km that burned on one local date, by day or by night. A fire that VIIRS sees as five pixels counts once.
steps.s3: Convert VIIRS to MODIS-equivalent. For each region, season, and day or night, the ratio of Aqua to VIIRS fire cell-passes in {from}–{to} becomes a weight on every VIIRS detection. Every number in the app is a sum of those weights. Only VIIRS is converted down; nobody can invent the small fires MODIS never saw.
steps.loyo: Three ways of setting the ratios were compared on the training years, leaving one year out at a time. Their typical errors were {c1}, {c2} and {c3}; the naive stitch scored {c0}. The simplest candidate within a tenth of the best was kept ({chosen}) and frozen before the test.

test.heading: 4. The test
test.design: The ratios were tuned on {trainFrom}–{trainTo} only. The years {testFrom} and {testTo} were kept aside until the method was frozen. On those years the harmonized VIIRS record is compared with what Aqua counted. The results were recomputed once, after a second review (by a separate AI session that had not written the code) changed which days count as outages; the frozen ratios did not change.
test.scatterCaption: Each dot is one province in one month of the test years. On the line, VIIRS equals Aqua. Both axes are logarithmic.
test.scatterLabel: Province-months of the test years: Aqua hotspots against VIIRS, raw and harmonized, on logarithmic axes. {n} province-months.
test.tableCaption: Test-year results at three scales, harmonized next to the naive stitch
test.notes: Bias is the total over or under Aqua’s. Typical error is the median absolute error, in percent. Correlation is taken on the logarithm of the counts. Only cases with at least 20 Aqua hotspots are scored.
test.targets: Targets set before the test: national bias within ±{biasMax}, province-month error at most {mapeMax}, national correlation at least {corrMin}.
test.peak: The busiest month of the year matched Aqua’s in {share} of {n} province-years.

beyond.heading: 8. Beyond the test
beyond.ratioText: The yearly ratio of Aqua to harmonized VIIRS was {first} in {firstYear} and {last} in {lastYear}. It was highest in {maxYear} ({max}) and lowest in {minYear} ({min}). A later Aqua overpass would raise it, and S-NPP’s outages in 2024 may add to that. The record reads high in months with little fire, which lowers the ratio in a quiet year. This page does not prove the cause.

beyond.ratioLabel: Yearly ratio of Aqua to harmonized VIIRS from {from} to {to}.
beyond.seamText: At the seam, from {from} to {to}, both sensors flew and the series switches from one to the other. Month by month the harmonized VIIRS total ran {bias} from Aqua’s, with a typical error of {mape} over {n} months.
beyond.seamCaption: National hotspots per month across the switch from MODIS to VIIRS
beyond.seamLabel: Monthly national totals from {from} to {to}: Aqua MODIS and harmonized VIIRS.

noaa20.heading: 9. A third satellite: NOAA-20
noaa20.text: S-NPP stopped delivering data on 2 November 2026. NOAA-20 carries the same VIIRS instrument in the same orbit and carries the record from {month}. Its ratios were fitted on {trainFrom}–{trainTo}, the stable years it shared with Aqua, and tested on the same held-out years.
noaa20.fill: NOAA-20 also stands in for S-NPP on {days} days since {year}: the days on which S-NPP delivered no data, or none by day. Those days carry NOAA-20’s harmonized counts. This was added after the held-out test and changes none of its results, which compare S-NPP alone with Aqua.
noaa20.textFuture: S-NPP stopped delivering data on 2 November 2026. NOAA-20 carries the same VIIRS instrument in the same orbit and will carry the record from November 2026. Its ratios are already fitted, on {trainFrom}–{trainTo}, the stable years it shared with Aqua, and tested on the same held-out years.
noaa20.caption: NOAA-20: the held-out test against Aqua, and the handover check against harmonized S-NPP

limits.heading: 10. Limits
items: Satellites miss fires under cloud or thick smoke, and small or short fires between passes.
“MODIS-equivalent” undercounts small fires by design. The raw VIIRS detections are still in the hotspots CSV.
Hotspot counts are not burned area.
Drawn areas and circles are resolved at about 5 km.
Harmonized values carry a typical error, larger for small counts and for single provinces.
Fixed heat sources labelled as fire inflate the VIIRS era in a few provinces.
Where the record runs into the current year, its latest months use near-real-time data, which is revised later.
This is a record of the past and a measure of how unusual a month is. It is not a forecast.
limits.extremePct: Extreme months are understated: about {pct} low at 5 times the usual level or more.
limits.noaa20Provinces: In {count} of {total} provinces NOAA-20’s gap to Aqua in the test years differs from S-NPP’s by more than 10 points (the most in {name}: S-NPP {snpp}, NOAA-20 {noaa}). There the months NOAA-20 carries, from {month} and on the days it fills, can sit above or below the S-NPP months.

data.heading: Data and credits
items: NASA FIRMS MODIS Collection 6.1 active fire detections (Aqua).
NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375 m active fire detections (S-NPP and NOAA-20).
Optional map layer: SAOCOM L-band radar mosaics, 2022, CONAE (Argentina’s space agency).
Designing and building was assisted with Claude, an AI assistant (Anthropic)
data.excluded: {days} days are left out of every comparison: the days on which one of the sensors delivered no data, and a window from 16 August to 2 September 2020 that was set aside before the test as a suspected Aqua outage. Today’s archive has Aqua data on most of those days, so leaving them out is only a precaution.

trends.text: Province by province, the same thing happens. Raw counts rise in {rawRising} of {total} provinces, because VIIRS reports several detections where MODIS reported one. The harmonized record rises in {rising}, falls in {falling}, shows no significant trend in {none} and has too little fire to assess in {unrated}.
trends.caption: Trend of the yearly totals by province: harmonized record and raw counts
trends.note: The last column is a check, not a correction. Where a province’s harmonized record ran more than 15% from MODIS in the test years, its trend is tested again with that gap taken out of every VIIRS year. No count in the app changes. Raw percentages run very high where the record started from very little fire.
trends.check: A check that does not lean on the method. From {from} to {to}, Aqua MODIS alone, the same sensor all along: {aqua}. The harmonized record: {harmonized}. Aqua’s orbit has drifted to a later overpass, nearer the afternoon peak of fire, so its last years may read high and this check, if anything, understates the fall. It supports the national trend but does not prove it.
